mention.lead_sentence: We here propose a general nodes map of applied nodes (figure1)

items.note: The paper's node map, and it is a scatter pretending to be a map: 4,295 nodes drawn as latitude/longitude points with NO basemap, no coastline and no state outline - the continental US shape emerges only from point density. x 'longitude' -120 to -70, y 'latitude' 25 to 50, both with numeric ticks and no grid. Legend INSIDE upper-right with three keys: major cities (red filled dot), destination chargers (green plus), super chargers (blue asterisk). No title, no colourbar, nothing 3-D, no data labels. Caption 27.6 pt below and it misspells 'inclueded'. The caption is three thousand nodes wide and the legend is the only thing that separates the three populations, which is why the caption has to name all three.

The zoom of Figure 1 at one city, same three-key legend INSIDE upper-right, same bare lat/lon axes but two orders of magnitude finer: x longitude -86.95 to -86.60 at 0.05 steps, y latitude 36.00 to 36.35. Two annotation circles are DRAWN on the plot - an inner red ring and an outer blue ring around one city marker - and neither is labelled, so the rings' radius is unreadable without the prose. In-plot title 'Salt Lake City, UT'. The defect is worth keeping: those coordinates are the Nashville, TN area (-86.8, 36.2), while Salt Lake City is (-111.9, 40.8) - title, caption and data contradict each other, and the caption 'Nodes around Salt-Lake City' inherits the error.

mention.lead_sentence: For the Allocation of chargers, the distribution map can be seen in Figure 3.

items.note: The US half of the paper's surface/contour pair: a perspective surface mesh of charger demand over longitude -130 to -60 and latitude 20-55, vertical axis 0 to 25000 in 5000 steps, a flat dark-blue base plane with 25 to 35 narrow spikes and a red/orange maximum near 25000. Grid walls are drawn on three panes, so the crop confirms a perspective surface mesh - the only 3-D family in the paper. No title, no legend, no colourbar (the fill is a colormap over height and carries no scale of its own), no data labels. The measured box CLIPS the framed box on all four sides (ink spans about 163-422 by 398-638 pt against a bbox of 179-413 by 413-618), which is why the region is smaller than the artwork. Caption 45.6 pt below - the second-widest gap in the paper.

mention.lead_sentence: The charger connections can be seen in Figure 4.

items.note: The charger NODE CLOUD of the United States: several hundred magenta dots over longitude -120 to -70 and latitude 25-50, no basemap, no state outlines - the country's shape is drawn by point density alone, exactly as in Figure 1 but scaled to the whole network and with a single marker class. No legend, no title, no grid, no colourbar, flat. The caption says 'Connections' and the plot draws ZERO edges: no lines join any two nodes, so the word describes an intention the artwork does not show. Caption 29.3 pt below, and the prose that cites it ('The charger connections can be seen in Figure 4.') prints a page EARLIER, on p13.

note:
**Coverage.** Twenty-nine pages, twenty measured regions on fifteen of them, all accounted
once: twelve figure rows, two table rows and six excluded regions. Nineteen captions, of
which only fourteen print on region-bearing pages - the other five are tables that print
as text.

**This paper's tables are not tables.** Tables 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 print as bare text laid
out in loose columns: no frame, no rules, no zebra, no header band. Table 3 on p15 is
literally one text block from y92.3 to y201.5 - caption and six body rows in a single
block, the caption's glyph boxes overlapping the first row by 1.5 pt - and the page has
exactly one drawing object on it (the running header rule). So the region pass has nothing
to box, and a caption-plus-text detector would have to invent the grid. Only Tables 5 and
6, on p17, are ruled, and both are ruled as closed boxes: outer frame, vertical rules
between every column, horizontal rules between every row.

**The model half pastes its mathematics.** All three regions on pp6-8 are text: a prose
paragraph with the Notations definition list (p6), the bulleted specification of the
minimum-cost max-flow model (p7, 457x353 pt, the largest box before the results) and four
numbered display equations (p8). The '2.4 Demand Estimation Model' heading prints 4 pt
under the p7 box - a heading weld that any caption rule would misread. p10 repeats the
pattern with the Nash payoff displays (EX1 to EX4, whose EX1 and EX2 print byte-identical
right-hand sides).

**Every exhibit is caption-only art.** Twelve figures, no in-plot titles anywhere, printed
numbers limited to axis ticks, no data labels, no colourbar - and the same field drawn
twice per country. The paper's whole quantitative story is: a node cloud, a surface, a
contour, per country. The two contours (Figures 5 and 8) carry no colourbar, so half of
each pair is unquantified; the two node clouds captioned 'Connections' (Figures 4 and 6)
draw zero edges; and the 3-D surfaces are the paper's only three-dimensional work, with
grid walls on three panes.

**Caption geography.** All fourteen captions print below. Gaps run from 10.6 pt (Table 6)
to 58.3 pt (Figure 7), and the wide ones are not sloppiness - they follow the amount of
white space a box leaves in its column. Figure 7's 58.3 pt is wide enough that the caption
could be read as owning the white band above the box, which is why ownership on p16 is
argued from single-column alignment and from the fact that the page carries no body text
at all. p16 and p19 each put two captions in ONE text-layer unit, but only because neither
caption ends in a full stop - they print on separate lines 277 pt and 190 pt apart.

**Citation is forecast-first.** Eleven of fourteen rows are named by number, and six are
named before they print - Table 3 and Table 4 two pages early (p13 prose, p15 print),
Figures 4 and 5 one page early, Figures 9 to 12 one page early. Spacing is glued
('figure1', 'Table3', 'Figure10'), which is a text-layer hazard worth recording: the label
and the number never separate. Two captions are silently wrong about their own content:
Figure 2 is titled 'Salt Lake City, UT' and captioned 'Nodes around Salt-Lake City', but
its coordinates (-86.8, 36.2) are Nashville, TN; and Figure 6's caption says
'Connections', its prose says 'location', and its ink is a point cloud.

**Apparatus limits worth keeping.** A red Chinese resale banner prints at the top of ALL
29 pages (y29.5-39.5, full width), not just the raster pages, so `caption_above` is that
banner on every page that opens with a box. Table 6's caption runs straight into a body
sentence - 'Table 6: Best Profit Model Derivation value of 0.375, the value of P0 should
be stable at 0.275.' - so an eighteen-word caption is recorded where the paper intended a
title. Table 4's caption prints 'andRural' with no space, Figure 1's says 'inclueded',
Table 3 says 'Huston' and 'Atalanta'. And the two appendix regions are not exhibits at
all: p27's is a rule-bracketed red heading ('Linear Programming', 11.1 pt, between two
0.6 pt rules at y474.1 and y499.9) and p29's is the header rule, one code line
('print "time consumed: %s s" % (stop - start)') and the rule that closes the block.


Excluded regions, one line each.
p6r1: A 459x240 pt PASTE of body prose and a definition list, not artwork: 'Equation (2) presented the non-negativity of demand sharing in two nodes...', then the Notations entries V, E, G, d_i, c_i, d(i,j) and y_ij ending '...but finally charged in j.' The next line, 'alpha: A Dimensionless Coefficient of long distance traveling.', starts at about 571 pt - 7 pt under the box - so the block is cut out of a running paragraph. No axes, no numbers to plot, no caption.
p7r1: A 457x353 pt PASTE of a bulleted specification list for the minimum-cost max-flow model: 'Assume that the network flow model is G_net = (V_net, E_net)...' down through the four dashed conclusions ending '- The optimal c_i equals the flow of edge (vc_i, T);'. It is the largest measured box in the paper's model half and it is a list, not a figure. The '2.4 Demand Estimation Model' HEADING is what prints 4 pt under its bottom edge - a heading weld, not a caption.
p8r1: A 445x154 pt PASTE of four numbered display equations: the demand-function lead-in 'Therefore, We propose the demand function subjected to the location of each node:' and (8) to (11) with their numbers flush right at x~545-562 pt, which is what pushed the measured box past the text measure. Body prose resumes 36 pt below. No axes, no caption.
p10r1: A 430x191 pt PASTE of the Nash-equilibrium payoff derivation: the italic lead-in 'formulation from Nash Equilibrium provides' over five centred unnumbered displays (EX1 = (P0/P)((P-P0)/P0)^2 through EX4 and EX = sum_i EX_i). No axes, no rule, no grid, no caption. It is the trap of the page pair because Table 1 and Table 2 BOTH print on this page and NEITHER owns a region: their captions sit at y653.6 and y723.5, i.e. 328 and 398 pt BELOW this box, and each is a three-column, one-header, two-row grid with no rules, no frame and no zebra. So p10 presents one of the paper's twelve figures-to-be as an equation strip and two of its seven tables as unruled text. Defect inside the box: EX1 and EX2 print byte-identical right-hand sides.
p27r1: A 423x26 pt SECTION HEADING, not an exhibit and not even code: two black 0.6 pt rules at y474.1 and y499.9 bracket a red 11.1 pt title 'Linear Programming', indented 17 pt. It is one of the appendix's red sub-headings inside 'Appendix A Code' (the sibling 'Build Graph' sits on p24), so the region pass boxed a rule-bracketed heading between two code lines. No caption, no figure number, and 423 x 26 pt is exactly the rule width the detector followed.
p29r1: The last measured box in the paper, 423x42 pt, is page furniture around one code line: the running-header rule at y61.4, the closing code line 'print "time consumed: %s s" % (stop - start)' in 9 pt monospace navy, and the rule that closes the coding block at y103.4. Three items, two of them rules; the page is otherwise 90 per cent blank. The paper ends on a print statement.
rules: Twenty measured regions on fifteen of twenty-nine pages resolve to FOURTEEN exhibit rows - twelve figures and two tables - plus six excluded regions, and every region is claimed exactly once [place.doc_order].

The six exclusions are all text, not artwork: three model-half pastes on pp6-8 (prose, a bulleted flow-model specification and four numbered displays) and three appendix fragments on pp10, 27 and 29 (the Nash payoff derivation, a rule-bracketed 'Linear Programming' heading, and page furniture around one line of code) [geometry.family].

Five captioned exhibits own NO region and are recorded as declared gaps rather than invented rows: Tables 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 all print as bare unruled text with no table object at all, so the region pass sees a caption-plus-text block and never a grid [caption.verbatim].

Placement splits cleanly at the paper's halfway point: six rows sit in the modelling sections 2.3-2.7 (where three of the model's own regions are text, not figures) and eight sit in the results sections 4.1-4.4 [place.section_path].

Section kind follows the same split - two test rows under Shortest Path, twelve rows in the 4.x result tasks that the heading detector types as `other` - so no row is typed as `result` even though eight of them report results [place.section_kind].

Rows spread evenly down the page rather than clustering: six in the top third, six in the middle and two at the foot, and no exhibit takes a page - the largest single box covers 11.6 per cent of its page [place.page_zone].

Nothing is solo-page and the mean row covers 6.7 per cent of its page; the two rows that come closest to a full page are the tall portrait boxes of Figures 6 and 7, both of which are single charts with no panels [place.area_frac].

Caption side is UNIFORM here and does not track exhibit kind: all twelve figure captions sit BELOW their box and both table captions sit BELOW their grid - the only paper in this stretch where a table caption and a figure caption take the same side [caption.position].

But the gaps do not track kind either, and they are wide: 10.6 and 10.8 pt for the two tables, and 17.7 to 58.3 pt for the figures, with Figure 7's 58.3 pt the widest caption gap recorded in this census so far [caption.verbatim].

Numbering is one spelling throughout - 'Figure N:' and 'Table N:', a space after the label, a colon after the number - on all fourteen quoted captions, which makes this the most consistent caption spelling in the run [caption.numbering].

Captions are bare noun phrases and short: five words at the minimum, seven at the median, ten at the longest among figures, one sentence each, and only Table 6 runs to eighteen words because it swallows a body sentence [caption.words].

No caption states a unit, names a variable, gives a condition or draws a conclusion - voice is `none` on all fourteen - so the paper's reading load sits entirely in the prose sentences that precede each exhibit [caption.voice].

Family mix is two pairs plus one-off: five scatter rows, two 3-D surfaces, two filled contours, two line charts and one schematic - and the two surfaces and two contours are the same two fields (US demand, Korean demand) drawn twice each [geometry.family].

Legends are the exception, not the rule: nine of twelve figures carry none, and the three that do (Figures 1, 2 and 12) put them INSIDE the plot area, twice upper-right for the node map and its zoom, once lower-left for the six-country weight scatter [geometry.legend].

No colourbar anywhere - including the two filled contours, whose fill levels are therefore unreadable from the page - so a colourbar detector looking for a ramp beside a filled chart would report two that do not exist [geometry.colorbar].

Two rows are three-dimensional and they are the surface halves of the two pairs: Figures 3 and 7 are perspective surface meshes with grid walls on three panes, the only 3-D rows in the paper, and their contour partners are flat [geometry.three_d].

Panels are absent: panel_count is 1 on all fourteen rows, nothing is a panel of anything, and the paper splits a paired reading into TWO numbered figures rather than one two-panel chart - twice over, for the US and for Korea [geometry.panel_count].
Printed numbers are axis furniture everywhere: every row carries numeric ticks, no row prints a value on the data itself, so the paper has no data labels at all [geometry.printed_numbers].

Both measured grids are CLOSED BOXES - a full frame plus vertical rules between every column and horizontal rules between every row - which lands them in the `vertical-rules` bucket and makes this paper the inverse of the booktabs habit [table.rule_style].

Neither grid is striped and neither carries a merged cell, a diagonal header or a continued table; both are transposed layouts where a repeated 'Location | Numbers' row pair carries two stacked five- or six-city blocks instead of one long column [table.rows].

Grid size follows the data: Table 5 is four body rows by six columns (two five-city blocks) and Table 6 is five body rows by seven columns (one year row plus four quantity rows), so both are two to three times wider than they are tall [table.cols].

Header treatment is a single header row on both grids, and on Table 6 the header is a YEAR ROW rather than a label row - 2012 to 2017 - so the grid is read as a time series turned sideways [table.header_rows].

No grid prints a unit in its header or in a column: quantity is carried by the caption ('Number of Chargers') and by row labels, and percentage-like values print as bare decimals, which is why Table 6's two ratio rows are the only decimal-aligned columns in the paper [table.units_in_header].
Decimal alignment is real but narrow: the P_e and P_0 rows of Table 6 align on two places, while the count rows above them and all of Table 5 are centred as strings [table.decimal_aligned].

Widths stop short of the measure on both grids - 311 pt for Table 5 and 333 pt for Table 6, i.e. 52 and 56 per cent - and the five unmeasured tables print narrower still at about 195 to 330 pt [table.width].

Citation is real but forecast-led: eleven of fourteen rows carry a numbered reference in the prose, and six of those name the exhibit one or two pages BEFORE it prints, which is why this paper's lead_pages are mostly negative [mention.style].
Only three rows are never named at all: Figure 2, Figure 8 and Table 5, so the census cannot use the citation trail to find the paper's exhibits and neither could a reader [mention.first_page].

The reference spelling is glued - 'figure1', 'Table3', 'Figure10', 'Figure11' - and one is broken across a line as 'Fig- ure 7', so a regex looking for 'Figure \d' finds most of them and a regex looking for a space finds almost none [mention.lead_sentence].

Eleven rows quote a lead sentence and none quotes a trail sentence: this paper puts every reading in front of the exhibit ('We here propose a general nodes map of applied nodes (figure1)', 'to find an optimized solution(Table 6).') and never explains the figure afterwards [mention.trail_sentence].
Counts are one everywhere: no exhibit is referenced twice anywhere in the paper, not even the two contour figures that are the second half of a pair [mention.count].

Lead distance is the paper's own habit, not a census artefact: six of the fourteen rows are named exactly one page before they print (Figures 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 12 minus those that print on their own page), and the paper's only two-page lead belongs to Tables 3 and 4, promised on p13 and printed on p15 - which is exactly why they own no row and the oversized lead had to be declared rather than measured [mention.lead_pages].

tables.note: The game-theory calibration grid: five rows by seven columns with the 'Year' row doing the header's work (2012 to 2017), then 'EV Purchase' 52607...199826, 'Chargers' 11042...59167, and the two italic-math rows P_e 0.11...0.59 and P_0 0.21...0.30. Same CLOSED-BOX ruling as Table 5 (frame plus every internal rule), no zebra, no merged cell, no diagonal, no unit. The two ratio rows are decimal-aligned on two places while the two count rows are not, so decimal alignment holds only where the data is fractional. 333 pt wide. Caption 10.6 pt below the grid, and that caption is the paper's cleanest apparatus fault: it reads 'Table 6: Best Profit Model Derivation value of 0.375, the value of P0 should be stable at 0.275.' - the title runs straight into a full body sentence and takes the 0.375 / 0.275 finding with it, so an eighteen-word caption is recorded where the paper intended two.
